verdict.rationale: Fivetran's docs state that each pre-built connector handles incremental syncs automatically with no pipelines to maintain, and that deletes are captured. Community users describe syncing as very reliable, though one reports occasional out-of-sync states that required full re-syncs, which Fivetran did for free. Missing for 10: detailed first-party documentation of the cursor/state mechanism (e.g., how it works per connector type), and independent hands-on confirmation that only changed rows move.

support.subject: As a data engineer, syncs move only new and changed records — cursor and state management handled for me, not full reloads

citations.quote: Each connector handles schema changes, API updates, and incremental syncs automatically — no data pipelines to maintain.
Capture deletes | YES | `ENTITY` table and its child tables
Fivetran's syncing has been very reliable (compared to others we tried)
